build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not picture 74: its packed bytes end on the disk where picture 75's packed bytes begin, and the unpacker reads on to the end of its 3-sector window, so these are those bytes decoded with picture 74's value table (side 4's, this snapshot's). Nothing reads them

comments.text: Picture 74's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$0060, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$0027, channel 2's script at +$003A and channel 3's script at +$004A.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 8 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 7, frame 1 then 15, frame 2 then 1, frame 3 then 5, frame 3 then 1, frame 3 then 20, frame 3 then 10, frame 2 then 3. One pass takes 62 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 6 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 4 then 1, frame 5 then 1, frame 6 then 1, frame 7 then 1, frame 7 then 1, frame 8 then 1. One pass takes 6 steps.

Channel 2's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 5 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 4 then 1, frame 9 then 1, frame 10 then 1, frame 11 then 1, frame 12 then 1. One pass takes 5 steps.

Channel 3's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 7 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 4 then 1, frame 13 then 2, frame 14 then 5, frame 15 then 2, frame 16 then 3, frame 17 then 3, frame 18 then 2. One pass takes 18 steps.

Picture 74's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $06 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 33 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 74, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1 and 2: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 26 bitmap bytes in all (1 run of a repeated byte among them), in columns 8 to 10. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 74, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 3 and 8: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 20 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 8 to 10. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 3 of picture 74, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 4, 5, 6 and 7: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 22 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 9 to 10. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 74, named by channel 1's entry 1, channel 2's entry 1 and channel 3's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 5 of picture 74, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entry 2: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 13 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
